turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So yeah, I've just been having a cough for the last week and I think I had a little bit of a fever in the last few days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you said the cough started a week ago?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, around a week ago OK and the fever started two to three days ago. Yeah, I haven't really measured it, but like I definitely have been feeling chills.I've been wearing like multiple blankets over the last few days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok, have you taken your temperature? You said you haven't taken your temperature right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So let's focus on the cough. Is it persistent or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think the cough is pretty persistent over the last week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does it get worse with like cold air or dust? Like maybe pets or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think it stays around the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, umm, does it get better with anything? Have you tried any over the counter cough syrup?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I tried tylenol cold and liked it. I think it made it a bit better, like it helped me sleep. Other than that, during the day, it's still around the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how would you describe this cough? Is it barky? Is it harsh? Does it sound muffled?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: How I would say is that it's kind of like it's not too harsh. It's more like a wet cough. I'm definitely bringing up some some sputum.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, what color is the sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's usually like a, uh like a white and sometimes like a little bit yellow as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, is it ever green or do you ever see blood in there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't seen any of that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you ever had a cough like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, yeah, probably like in the last year, maybe I have gotten sick like once and had a similar cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you have a sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't have a sore throat.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Is this cough getting worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's, I think not really, it stayed around the same and I definitely feel a bit better with the tylenol cold.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good. Any changes in your taste or smell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no changes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in hearing or vision?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And did you have in the past week a runny or stuffy nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any weight loss over the past month?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no, not really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about changes in your hair, nails or skin like rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no changes to the skin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about wheezing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think I've recently.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No chest pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about swelling? Have you noticed any swelling in like your legs or arms or your belly area?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about you feeling like your heart's racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about a calf pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Confusion or memory loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have your bowel movements been normal?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I like go three times a day and I don't have any diarrhea or anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about urinating wise?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Everything normal there. Yeah, no trouble.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK,nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Joint pain or muscle ache?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any Contacts with sick people around you recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My wife was actually just sick last week, but she recovered. She did have a fever for one of the days and she also had a cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, did she get it checked out in a clinic?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so. She did get that COVID test done, but it came back negative and she didn't go to the doctor or anything. It kind of just went away on its own.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any travel recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Are you otherwise healthy? Do you have any longstanding medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just as a child. I had, probably in my teens, had my appendix removed, but nothing other than that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, no hospitalizations other than that too, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Are you on any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I just take some multi vitamins.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you up to date with all your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, as far as I know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do have like some, I get some runny nose around spring time probably I think I'm allergic to pollen.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any family history of lung conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think my father has high blood pressure if that's like a heart condition.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sure. And how old was he when he got that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: He's around like 60s right now, so probably like in his 40s.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any cancers in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do have an aunt on my mother's side who had ovarian cancer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how old was she when she was diagnosed with ovarian cancer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think probably in her 50s.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't smoke.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Marijuana just maybe like one or two joints in a month, just when I'm feeling that I need to relax a little.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sure and by joint, you said once a month right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, once per month.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any other drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no other drugs.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And where do you live right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live in London right now. I live with my wife in an apartment.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any reasons to think you have old carpet mold or asbestos?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, it's a fairly new apartment.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and well those are all the questions that I had for you today. Did you have any questions for me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You don't think it could be COVID right? Like my wife got tested and it was negative.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Are you concerned about that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, for sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Honestly, some of your symptoms do seem to be overlapping with that of COVID, especially the cough and fever. So we are going to do a COVID swab just to rule that out. So you will get those results in 24 to 48 hours and you should isolate for 14 days because your symptoms overlap. Public health will be in touch with you if it's positive just to do some contact tracing. But if it's not COVID, it could be another viral infection that's going around at this time of year so keep an eye on your symptoms. If they become worse, or if you're experiencing symptoms like neurological deficits or weakness or seizures or anything like that, get help from the ER right away and if your symptoms are persisting beyond like seven days to 10 days, also you should give us a call back to see what's going on because it could be something like a bacterial infection, in which case we can give you some antibiotics. Does that sound OK?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, great. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Thank you.
